A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CFGen, with the same authors, core framework and shared experiments despite the revised title. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original single-cell generation comparisons, multi-modal experiments, compositional guidance demonstrations and rare-cell augmentation results in Section 5 and Appendix I.

after.justification: V2 retains original generation and augmentation results and adds batch correction, imputation, runtime measurements and sensitivity analyses in Section 5.5 and Appendix H.

M1.justification: The core autoencoder, flow objective and compositional guidance algorithms remain. V2 adds substantial inference adaptations: inverse/forward flow transport to a reference batch for correction (Section 5.5), and masked-data imputation through inversion, Gaussian perturbation and regeneration (Appendix H.6).

E1.justification: V2 retains the original dataset coverage and adds the C. Elegans atlas. It introduces batch-correction evaluation on C. Elegans and NeurIPS, plus masked-count imputation on four retained datasets, substantially broadening the evaluated tasks and input conditions.

E2.justification: V2 adds scANVI and scPoli for batch correction, scDiffusion and RNA-only CFGen to the PBMC10K comparison, and scVI/scDiffusion augmentation comparisons in Figure A10. Figure 2 additionally evaluates scGAN. The original Table 1 comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 replaces linear MMD with RBF-kernel MMD using five scales and removes Table 1's generated-cell kNNc F1 evaluation. New protocols include 50-dimensional scIB batch-correction evaluation, 10% masking for imputation, CellTypist augmentation evaluation and classifier-based quantitative guidance assessment. These are substantive evaluation changes.

E4.justification: V2 adds runtime sensitivity to data and architecture sizes, RNA-only versus multi-modal CFGen comparisons, augmentation checks with CellTypist, imputation-noise sensitivity, quantitative guidance sweeps and analyses of excessive-guidance collapse. Appendix H.9 also examines library-size variation within HLCA studies.

E5.justification: Figure 2a adds fitted trends with shaded bands to existing mean-variance scatter comparisons, extending their statistical presentation. Tables 1–2 retain three-generation-seed averaging and variability reporting. The new bands' construction is unspecified, and no increase in repeated runs is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace MMD results under the changed kernel and revise Wasserstein entries; for example, conditional CFGen's Dentate gyrus distance changes from 18.74 to 21.55. V2 also adds substantial batch-correction, runtime, augmentation, imputation and guidance results. The MMD revisions are not directly comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 and its main argument are retained. Appendix B.4 corrects the diffusion coefficient's sigma_t factor to sigma_t squared, while Appendix B.1 corrects the Gamma scale description to mu/theta and restricts its shape parameter to positive values. These are limited mathematical corrections.

C1.justification: V1 centers its contributions on discrete generation, compositional guidance and rare-cell augmentation. V2 explicitly elevates batch correction into the abstract, contribution list and conclusion, and newly claims novelty for its probabilistic factorization in Section 4.1, materially extending the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: V2 explains size-factor conditioning, separate-training stability and sampling-speed differences. It adds substantive limitations: separate training can be inefficient and memory-intensive; excessive guidance can improve scIB scores while collapsing biological variation; excessive imputation noise destroys cell-specific information. The original independence-assumption warning remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds training/generation runtime tables, runtime hardware and configuration details, batch-correction training budgets and guidance-selection instructions. Appendix A newly advertises preprocessed-dataset links alongside code. However, v1's general 80/20 cell split, Python version and detailed GPU-server inventory are no longer disclosed; core model hyperparameters remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendices B.5–B.6 and D.5 substantially develop CFGen's positioning against VAEs and scDiffusion, emphasizing conditional priors, library-size dependence and guidance mechanisms. Batch correction is related to invertible translation and diffusion style transfer, with additional relevant citations. Publication and citation-style updates alone are not counted.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, mathematical exposition, experimental descriptions and baseline explanations. It separates quantitative and qualitative evaluation narratives, reorganizes appendix material, moves algorithms into Appendix G, and adds ethics and reproducibility statements. These changes exceed the accompanying scientific additions.

P2.justification: V2 revises the overview diagram and Figure 2, restructures Tables 1–2, and adds substantial batch-correction, runtime, imputation and sensitivity displays. The original multi-modal Figure 3 is recolored and relocated to Figure A7; earlier generation and marker plots are retained and reorganized rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for central claims: formerly qualitative compositional guidance gains quantitative validation, and augmentation is tested against competing generators and with a second classifier. Batch correction and imputation include useful failure-condition analyses, improving practical guidance. Small mathematical corrections also help. These gains outweigh the limited reproducibility drawback from removing general split and hardware disclosures; changed MMD values are not themselves evidence of improved performance.
